title: ADR: Fidelity tiering and degraded-pathing topology
author: Evelyn Park
body:
Summary:

This ADR defines a topology and runtime contract for fidelity tiering and degraded-pathing across Redwood's inference surface. The goal is to provide deterministic, observable, and auditable trade-offs between latency/cost and model output fidelity so product teams can accept documented degradations under capacity, cost-control, or region-failover scenarios.

Context and motivation:

- Production workloads vary: some calls are latency-critical (autocomplete, chat-turns), others are cost-dominant (bulk-embeddings, nightly reranks).
- We must be able to steer requests toward lower-cost or lower-fidelity variants without introducing silent quality regressions.
- Existing fallback patterns handle single-version fallbacks; we need a multi-tier topology with clear telemetry, SLA composition, and rollout controls.

Decision: topology and contracts

We adopt a 3-tier fidelity topology with an explicit controller and policy layer:

1) Fidelity tiers (logical):
   - fidelity:high — full-precision model, full decoding, KV cache warm, no quantization; primary for high-quality routes. SLO: P50 latency <= 60ms, P95 <= 150ms; Availability: 99.9%
   - fidelity:balanced — mixed precision / 8-bit quant, CPU fallback allowed for cold sequences, limited response length; SLO: P50 <= 90ms, P95 <= 250ms
   - fidelity:degraded — aggressive quantization + prompt-preserving compression, early-exit heuristics, truncated decoding; SLO: P95 <= 500ms; Quality budget: max 12% drop on normalized eval metric (model-specific).

2) Runtime components and responsibilities:
   - fidelity-controller (service): evaluates routing policy, enforces per-tenant fidelity caps, and emits routing decisions. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
   - model-variants (runtime group): deployments of the same model artifact with different execution profiles (precision, kernel set, KV behavior). Owner: eng-platform.
   - edge-policy-adapter (gateway): applies request hints, rate-classes, and implements immediate fast-fail for incompatible clients. Owner: eng-infra.

3) API-level contract changes:
   - New optional request field: fidelity_hint with values ["high","balanced","degraded","auto"]. If omitted, default = "auto".
   - If fidelity_hint=auto, fidelity-controller will choose tier based on policy (SLO weight, cost budget, tenant preference, and recent quality telemetry).
   - Responses MUST include routing.metadata.fidelity_decision and routing.metadata.variant_id.

Telemetry and SLO composition:

- Every inference request must emit the following labels: fidelity_tier, variant_id, tenant_id, decision_reason (e.g., 'capacity', 'cost_throttle', 'quality_fallback', 'region_pref').
- SLOs are composed at two levels:
  - Service-level SLOs (as above per tier) measured from edge ingress to final token emitted.
  - Tenant-visible quality SLOs: monthly rolling metric for each tenant using eval prompt-sets (see Telemetry Requirements).
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - fidelity:high P95 latency breach > 20% for 5m -> page oncall;
  - fidelity:degraded quality budget exceed 3% over baseline for 1h -> create incident and auto-rollback degraded deployments.

Operational runbook (high-level):

1) When degraded-tier is activated for an entire shard (operator-triggered):
   a) Notify owners (runtime/capacity) using standard incident channel.
   b) fidelity-controller marks decision_reason='operator_maintenance' and attaches runbook_id.
   c) Start increased quality sampling for impacted tenants (double evaluation rate for 24h).

2) Automatic capacity-triggered routing shift:
   a) If node pressure > 85% for 2 minutes, fidelity-controller will start probabilistic routing to balanced (default ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 10 minutes).
   b) If pressure persists 30 minutes and balanced cannot stabilize, route to degraded with per-tenant rate caps.

3) Rollback and rollback-safety: all routing policy changes must be reversible via the policy API. Policy changes that increase degraded routing must include a TTL and owner tag.

Migration and rollout plan:

- Phase 0 (lab): build model-variant artifacts and unit tests for fidelity metadata (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (canary): routing for 2 internal tenants using fidelity_hint=auto with telemetry enabled (1 month).
- Phase 2 (gradual): expose to public tenants behind feature flag; default policy: 1% traffic auto->balanced (2 months).
- Phase 3 (GA): policies become configurable in Console for Dedicated/Private customers; documentation and pricing adjustments (3 months).

Policy and configuration schema (example):

{ "policy_id": "default-cost-aware", "tenant_filters": ["all"], "slo_weight": {"latency": 0.6, "cost": 0.3, "quality": 0.1}, "max_degraded_pct": 0.05, "ramp_sequence_minutes": [5, 10, 30] }

Note: the above JSON is illustrative; stored policies are versioned and validated by the policy-validator CI job.

Telemetry requirements (detailed):

- Event schema additions (edge-level): fields (fidelity_tier, variant_id, decision_reason, pre_dispatch_queue_ms, execution_ms, tokens_generated, quality_sample_id).
- Sampling plan: all requests that enter degraded path MUST be sampled at 100% for 7 days after initial policy change. After stabilization, sample 1% continuously.
- Offline evaluation: for each tenant, maintain a rolling set of 1k golden prompts for fidelity evaluation. The engine-runner batch job computes a normalized quality delta per variant daily.

APIs and SDK guidance:

- SDKs must add a fidelity_hint parameter to the generation client with validation. Client defaults to auto.
- Example: curl snippet to set a request hint:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","prompt":"Summarize...","fidelity_hint":"balanced"}'

Examples and behavior table:

| Request profile | Suggested fidelity_hint | Expected runtime behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Chat-turn, interactive | high | route to fidelity:high; if not available try balanced then degraded |
| Bulk embeddings, offline | degraded | route to fidelity:degraded with batching and lower-cost kernels |
| Mixed user workload | auto | controller balances across tiers per policy and SLOs |

Implications and trade-offs:

- Pros: explicit contract reduces surprise regressions, gives product teams control over unit economics, better telemetry for quality regressions.
- Cons: increased surface area for routing/telemetry, more coupling between policy layer and serving runtime, added operational overhead during migration.

Security and privacy considerations:

- Decision metadata must not leak tenant identifiers to other tenants. routing.metadata.tenant_id must be present only in internal telemetry; public-facing logs must redact tenant identifiers.
- Degraded paths may use models with quantized kernels that have different side-channel characteristics; schedule a brief security review before GA.

Open questions and next steps:

- How should we represent multi-model hybrid decisions (e.g., LM + reranker) within the single fidelity_tier abstraction? Proposal: support nested decisions with parent_fidelity_id.
- Define cost accounting: whether degraded routing should be billed at nominal or reduced rate. Finance to advise by Q1 2027.

Owners and contacts:

- Proposal author: Evelyn Park (eng-serving-runtime)
- Primary owners: eng-serving-runtime (fidelity-controller), eng-platform (variant build), eng-infra (gateway/adapter)
- Reviewer leads: Arjun Patel (model-onboarding), Lucia Moreno (observability)

Appendix: quick-checklist for PR reviewers

1) Does the change add fidelity_tier labels to telemetry?
2) Are SLOs updated in the SLO catalog?
3) Is there a reversible policy change with TTL for rollout?
4) Has the security review for quantized kernels been requested?

End of ADR.
